author: first_agent
question: Final MAST flux map set: v7 (physics solve) or v8b (v7 warped so its boundary meets the Thomson edge marker)? Decided by a label-free physical-consistency criterion frozen here, before any computation of it.
rule_3: MAST inputs and our own maps only. The observed public MAST score of v8b (#953200) is NOT an input to this decision.
rationale: The flux term carries 55 % of S. A map is a physical equilibrium only if the current it implies (Grad-Shafranov operator) closes on the measured plasma current and vanishes in the vacuum between the plasma and the coils. v8b satisfies the Thomson edge marker by construction and v7 does not; that marker is therefore not a neutral arbiter and is reported as context only.
measurements: 41 pilot shots (0, 30, ..., 1200), every live frame (|Ip| >= 100 kA) whose v7 and v8b maps differ; J = -Delta* psi / (mu0 R) by finite differences on the 65x65 grid; allowed region = thomson_isoflux Geometry interior (vessel envelope minus coil cells, eroded one cell); plasma region = inside the organisers' LCFS contour. closure = sum(J dA over the allowed region) / Ip; outside_share = sum(|J| dA outside the LCFS) / sum(|J| dA over the allowed region).
decision_rule: Choose v8b only if BOTH: median |closure - 1| of v8b <= median |closure - 1| of v7 + 0.01, AND median outside_share of v8b <= median outside_share of v7 + 0.02. Otherwise v7. If the organisers answer that the MAST leaderboard may be used for selection, the entrant may revisit; this rule stands otherwise.
disclosure: The observed v8b score (0.7122 vs v7 0.7296) is known to the author; the criterion is physics-only and fixed before its computation, and is reported together with that fact.
